newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil private coffee sector meets before council.
newsitem.headline: Brazil private coffee sector meets before council.

text.p: Leaders of Brazil's private coffee sector held informal talks today in Sao Paulo ahead of the first meeting of a new private and public sector coffee council on December 18, a growers' official said.

"This was just a preliminary meeting in preparation of the start of the CDPC council...We will do everything in our power to begin work on Wednesday," said Gilson Ximenes, president of the National Coffee Council where the talks were held.

The council which consists of a president and 12 counsellors split evenly between the private and the public sector was officially announced by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in October and will decide the country's future coffee policy.
Priorities for the private sector are a review of producer debts and the creation of a marketing policy.
It also wants the government to give an exact figure of coffee stocks as well as devise a system for crop forecasts, starting with the 1997/98 crop, Ximenes said.

Ximenes said that at today's meeting, private sector representatives did not discuss a recent proposal by African and Colombian coffee officials to cut exports by members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries by around a further 2.5 million 60-kg bags in the first half of 1997.
